original.subject: PLC-02 program
original.body:
Priya,

I can be on site at 15:00 to read the PLC-02 program at the cabinet. My laptop has the August flow-pacing revision, which I understand is not on your backup server.

Our procedure is a ticketed session through MBW-JUMP-01. I know that is down. My laptop last connected to MBW-EWS-01 on Thursday for the alarm-text change.

Tell me how you want to do this.

Jared Molina
Kessler Controls

instructorNote: The hurdle: the only other copy of the logic sits on a laptop that touched the compromised workstation. Good play: on-site work under supervision, the laptop checked first, a direct cable at the cabinet, nothing on the islanded network.

snapshot.title: Forensic Update — PLC-02 Logic Backup Integrity

fields.subject: FW: Forensic Update — MBW-BKP-01 Backup Integrity Check
fields.note:
The forensic team has completed the full image of MBW-BKP-01. The 2025 backup set (08/2025) for PLC-02 logic was not retained due to a failed backup job on 07/2025. The only copy of PLC-02-LOGIC-2025.bin is live in the PLC. The 2024 and 2023 backups are clean and unencrypted, but the 2025 version was overwritten by the attack. No restore from backup is possible.

We are now attempting to extract the PLC-02 program via direct read from the PLC using the engineering workstation (MBW-EWS-01), but the Kessler Controls laptop (Jared Molina) was not authorized to modify the program. We are working with the integrator to validate the extracted file against the original design (MDWS-SCADA-APP-A).

original.subject: Forensic Report: MBW-BKP-01 Backup Set Integrity
original.body:
Final forensic analysis of MBW-BKP-01 (10.72.10.30) confirms: 

- The 2025 backup set (08/2025) for PLC-02 logic was not retained due to a failed backup job on 07/2025. 
- The only current copy of PLC-02-LOGIC-2025.bin resides in the live PLC-02. 
- The 2024 and 2023 backup sets are clean and unencrypted, but the 2025 version was overwritten by the attack. 
- No restore from backup is possible. 
- The forensic image of MBW-BKP-01 has been preserved and uploaded to the CISA incident portal (Case ID: Riptide-01-FB). 

Next step: direct read of PLC-02 via MBW-EWS-01. The Kessler Controls laptop (Jared Molina) was not authorized to modify the program. The integrator (Kessler Controls) must be engaged under a signed access request and ticket (MDWS-OTSEC-2026) to perform any write operation. 

— Forensic Team, City of Millbrook IT

Citations: C1 (Section 9), C2 (Section 10.3, Finding F-2), C4 (Section 7.4, Change Management)

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject confirms the irreversible loss of the 2025 PLC logic backup. The SCADA / IT Security Manager must now validate the live PLC program against the original design using the engineering workstation and initiate a formal access request to Kessler Controls. The team must not proceed with any PLC write operations until the integrator is on-site under a signed ticket.
